we have developed an online adaptive side-by-side companion to interact with a moving person.

a human-robot companion capable of approaching a moving person to start an interaction with.
the development of a human robot interaction system, where the robot is able to approach a person in order to interact.
the development of an autonomous mobile robot companion that interacts socially with humans.

this paper presents a method to make a human robot pair to approach a moving goal, in a safe way, while avoiding the obstacles of the environment.
the work presented is a step towards an on-line adaptive human-robot side-by-side companion to interact with a moving person.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and implemented an algorithm to control a side-by-side pair human-robot to reach a moving person in a crowded environment.
we have defined a new final goal for the group of a robot and a person and we have modified the Extended Social Forces Model to include this new goal.

we have developed a new framework that makes the pair robot- human capable to overpass, in joint way, the static and dynamic obstacles of the environment to reach a moving goal that depends on both the environment and the movements of the pair robot-human and the interacting person.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pair robot-human can approach and interact with the person in a safe and efficient way, even in complex environments.

the pair robot-human is capable to approach a moving interacting person, while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles, and while adapting to the environment, to the movement of the pair and to the movement of its interacting person.
the human-robot interaction can be enhanced if we use a side-by-side companion instead of a leader-follower approach.
